ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle C=\angle D$, $OC=OD$. If $\angle O=72^\circ$, $\angle C=20^\circ$, and $\triangle OAD \cong \triangle OBC$; what is the degree measure of $\angle DAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $ \triangle OAD \cong \triangle OBC$,\\
$\therefore \angle C=\angle D=20^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC=\angle O+\angle D=20^\circ+72^\circ=\boxed{92^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use an exterior-angle route in triangle OAD. From the image, read that O, A, C are collinear with A on side OC, and O, B, D are collinear with B on side OD; segment AD is drawn, so angle DAC is the exterior angle at A of triangle OAD because AC is the extension of AO. From the text, read ∠O=72°, ∠C=20°, and triangle OAD is congruent to triangle OBC. By the congruence order OAD ≅ OBC, angle D of triangle OAD corresponds to angle C of triangle OBC, so ∠ODA=20°. Also ∠AOD is the same as the displayed apex angle ∠O, namely 72°. Apply the exterior angle theorem to triangle OAD: ∠DAC=∠AOD+∠ODA=72°+20°=92°.
